rule.description: Split assignment rule. Only 'hash' is defined in v1: a question is assigned by hashing seed + field value and bucketing against cumulative ratios.

field.description: Question key whose value is hashed for bucketing. Defaults to 'id'.

ratios.description: Fraction of unlabeled questions per split; the values must sum to 1.0.

seed.description: Any scalar; changing it deterministically reshuffles the hash assignment. Defaults to '0'.

splits.description: Dataset-level deterministic split rule applied to questions without an explicit per-question split label. Explicit labels always win over the rule; questions covered by neither land in both train and validation (back-compat, never test).

chat_message.description: One message in a multi-turn input. Matches Inspect AI's ChatMessage shape (role + content). Multimodal content parts and tool-call metadata are intentionally not modeled in v1; additionalProperties: true lets consumers carry them in transit.

input.description: A string or a list of chat messages. Chat mode sends messages natively. Agent and workflow modes receive a transcript of role: content lines separated by blank lines.

choices.description: Optional list of choices for multiple-choice evals. Matches Inspect AI's Sample.choices. Portable interchange shape — not all runners execute MCQ-style scoring natively.

files.description: Optional map of filename -> content/path/data-url. Input-side declaration matching Inspect AI's Sample.files. Portable artifact shape; ai_eval's current runtime does not stage files into a sandbox, and execution-environment fields (sandbox, setup) are out of scope for v1.

items.description: Expected retrieval page ids, such as node/108 or entity:node/108:en. Identical expectations merge; overlapping translation scopes are refused by the graders.

expected.description: Grader expectations. Any expected.<name> may hold reference text named by a target_match check through reference_path. Use a string or a list of alternative strings, including for field automator and taxonomy label outputs.

expected_tools.description: Assertions about the tools an agent ran while answering. Scored against the agent's own record of what it executed where the runtime exposes one; a runtime that exposes none may fall back to reading the response text, which can only answer `should_run`.

tool.description: The tool asserted on, by either of its names: the function name the model emits, or the implementation-side plugin id. A name containing a colon can only be a plugin id, since function names carry none; a bare name is checked against both.

should_run.description: Whether the tool must have run (true) or must not have (false).

args.description: Arguments the call must have carried, as a SUBSET: name only the ones the assertion is about, and any others the model passed are ignored. This is what distinguishes two calls to the same tool, which are otherwise identical. Values are compared as text, so 12 and "12" are the same assertion, except booleans and null, which compare strictly. Answerable only from a tool-call record; an implementation reading the response text instead cannot check it and MUST fail the expectation rather than score it as met. An empty object is rejected rather than read as an assertion about nothing, which would make that failure rule untrue of a document the schema accepted.

additionalProperties.description: Scalar only. A structured value cannot be asserted on: a record stores the shape of a non-scalar argument rather than the value, so such an assertion could never match.

after.description: Another tool that must have run before this one, named the same way as `tool`. Read as "by the time this ran, that had happened", compared on first occurrence of each. `args` narrows which call of THIS tool is meant; the named predecessor cannot be narrowed the same way, so any of its calls satisfies the ordering. Answerable only from a tool-call record, with the same failure rule as `args`. Must carry a non-whitespace character: a blank value asserts nothing while making the expectation read as an ordering check.

then.$comment: An ordering assertion on a tool that must NOT have run is incoherent: there is no call whose position could be compared. Rejected rather than accepted and ignored, which is the failure mode this schema exists to prevent.

disabled.description: When true, this question is excluded from evaluation runs. Loader implementations must filter out disabled questions before executing them.

split.description: Optional dataset split label; a labeled question belongs to that split only, so validation and test rows are held out from optimizer training. Unlabeled questions fall back to the dataset-level splits rule when present, else to both train and validation (back-compat).

bundle.description: Eval domain identifier, snake_case. Pattern matches the id convention used elsewhere; loader-side registered-bundle validation is Layer 3.

metadata.description: Case-level context. Templates may reference metadata keys. Submodules may define their own keys here, such as metadata.droost for ai_eval_droost.

inputs.description: Workflow input ports. These override fixed workflow_inputs and cannot name the question port. Search API reads k, conjunction, chunks, min_score and text. AI Automators reads source fields, such as body with value and format or a taxonomy reference list, and text_format. The portable form is a map. The runner also accepts a JSON object string internally, but dataset schema validation rejects that form. Agent and chat targets ignore these inputs.

caller_uid.description: Optional Drupal user ID. Overrides the run-level caller UID. The target invocation, including a workflow, runs as this account; graders keep the run account.

user_name.description: Optional display name. In every mode, [Caller: name] prefixes a string input or the first user message. Search API and AI Answers recommend omitting it because the prefix becomes query text.
